title: Subject pronouns, on, tu and vous
spec: Pronouns: personal: all subjects, including on; Verbs: modes of address: tu, vous
summary: The subject pronouns are je, tu, il, elle, on, nous, vous, ils, elles.
je becomes j' before a vowel or silent h: j'aime, j'habite.
il and elle also mean it, matching the gender of the noun: Le vélo ? Il est neuf. La voiture ? Elle est rouge.
ils is used for a group of males or a mixed group; elles only for an all-female group: Paul et Julie → ils.
on means we (very common in speech), one, or people in general, and always takes the il/elle form of the verb: on va, on mange.
tu is for one person you know well (friend, family member, child, pet).
vous is for one person you speak to politely (a stranger, a teacher, an adult you don't know) and for any group of people.
Once you choose tu or vous, keep it everywhere: ton / votre, te / vous (reflexive), lève-toi / levez-vous, s'il te plaît / s'il vous plaît.
Changing nous to on: nous allons → on va; nous jouons → on joue.

cards.front: List the nine French subject pronouns with their English meanings.
cards.back: je (I), tu (you, informal), il (he/it), elle (she/it), on (we/one/people), nous (we), vous (you, polite or plural), ils (they, masc. or mixed), elles (they, all female).

cards.prompt: Ma sœur et moi, ___ allons au collège à pied.
cards.en: My sister and I walk to school.
cards.why: Ma sœur et moi = we; the verb allons is the nous form.

cards.back: Before a vowel or a silent h: j'aime, j'écoute, j'habite. Not before a consonant: je joue, je vais, je suis.

cards.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with je instead of nous.
cards.why: je becomes j' before the silent h of habite; the verb changes to the je form.

cards.front: ils or elles: which do you use for a mixed group?
cards.back: ils. elles is only for an all-female group (or all feminine nouns). Marc et ses sœurs → ils; Léa et Chloé → elles. Even one male in a group of ten makes it ils.

cards.prompt: Ma tante et mon oncle ? ___ viennent ce week-end.
cards.en: My aunt and uncle? They're coming this weekend.
cards.why: A mixed group of male and female takes ils.

cards.prompt: Mes sœurs et ma mère ? ___ adorent faire du shopping.
cards.en: My sisters and my mother? They love going shopping.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a subject pronoun.
cards.prompt: **Le livre et la lampe** sont sur la table.
cards.why: A masculine and a feminine noun together count as masculine plural: ils.

cards.prompt: Où est ton vélo ? — ___ est dans le garage.
cards.en: Where's your bike? — It's in the garage.
cards.why: vélo is masculine, so 'it' is il.

cards.prompt: Tu aimes ma nouvelle robe ? — Oui, ___ est très jolie.
cards.en: Do you like my new dress? — Yes, it's very pretty.
cards.why: robe is feminine, so 'it' is elle.

cards.front: What can on mean, and which verb form does it take?
cards.back: on = we (very common in speech), one / you in general, or people / they in general. It always takes the il/elle form of the verb: On va au cinéma ? En France, on mange tard.

cards.prompt: Le week-end, on ___ souvent au parc avec nos copains.
cards.en: At the weekend we often go to the park with our friends.
cards.why: on always takes the third-person singular (il/elle) form of the verb: on va.

cards.prompt: En France, on ___ beaucoup de pain.
cards.en: In France, people eat a lot of bread.
cards.why: Here on means people in general; it still takes the il/elle form: on mange.

cards.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with nous instead of on.
cards.prompt: On joue au tennis le mercredi.
answers: Nous jouons au tennis le mercredi.
cards.why: on takes the il/elle form; nous takes the -ons form: on joue → nous jouons.

cards.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with on instead of nous.
cards.why: on meaning we takes the il/elle form of the verb: nous allons → on va.

cards.front: tu or vous: when do you use each?
cards.back: tu: one person you know well: a friend, a family member, a child, a pet. vous: one person you address politely (a stranger, shop assistant, teacher, older adult) and always for more than one person.

cards.instruction: You are now asking a stranger. Rewrite the question using vous.
cards.why: A stranger is addressed with vous, so the verb changes to the vous form: vous avez.

cards.instruction: You are now asking a friend. Rewrite the question using tu.
cards.prompt: Vous voulez venir au cinéma ce soir ?
answers: Tu veux venir au cinéma ce soir ?
Veux-tu venir au cinéma ce soir ?
Est-ce que tu veux venir au cinéma ce soir ?
cards.en: Do you want to come to the cinema tonight?
cards.why: A friend is addressed with tu, so the verb changes to the tu form: tu veux.

cards.instruction: You work at a hotel reception. Rewrite the sentence for a guest, using vous.
cards.prompt: Assieds-toi, s'il te plaît, et remplis ta fiche.
answers: Asseyez-vous, s'il vous plaît, et remplissez votre fiche.
Assoyez-vous, s'il vous plaît, et remplissez votre fiche.
cards.en: Please sit down and fill in your form.
cards.why: Everything linked to tu changes to vous: the imperatives (assieds-toi → asseyez-vous, remplis → remplissez), s'il te plaît → s'il vous plaît, and ta → votre.

cards.instruction: You are now asking a friend. Rewrite the question using tu.
cards.prompt: Vous vous occupez de votre chien tous les jours ?
answers: Tu t'occupes de ton chien tous les jours ?
T'occupes-tu de ton chien tous les jours ?
Est-ce que tu t'occupes de ton chien tous les jours ?
cards.en: Do you look after your dog every day?
cards.why: With tu, the reflexive pronoun becomes te (t' before a vowel), the verb takes the tu form, and votre becomes ton: tu t'occupes de ton chien.
